Aeschylus seems to have pronounced this with the first syllable short on account of metrical necessity: by which the rule of Phrynichus (in Bekker's Anecdota p. 51) about the first syllable of the adjective μανός [thin, loose] being long is not refuted.

μανόν [thin] means ἀραιόν [loose], as also Aeschylus (fr. 411) "ἓν μανοστήμοις πέπλοις [in loose-woven robes]," that is, ἀραιοῖς [loose]. Hesychius: μανοστήμοις [loose-woven]: ἀραιοστήμοις [loose-threaded].
